pr.title: fix ICE in pretty-printing `global_asm!`
pr.description:
fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/138260

since https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/137180, `global_asm!` gets a fake body, that the pretty printing logic did not know what to do with.

based on [#t-compiler/help > tests for MIR pretty printing](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/182449-t-compiler.2Fhelp/topic/tests.20for.20MIR.20pretty.20printing) I created `tests/ui/unpretty/mir` which seemed as good a place as any for a test. If there is a better place, let me know.

try-job: test-various
try-job: x86_64-apple-2
pr.author: folkertdev

processing.reason: The historical defect is not a runtime MIR value transformation: `write_mir_sig` in `compiler/rustc_middle/src/mir/pretty.rs` panicked with `bug!("Unexpected def kind {:?}", kind)` while formatting a MIR dump for a `DefKind::GlobalAsm` fake body. The `SimplifyLocals` pass is only the dump trigger; the actual `SimplifyLocals` transformation is unchanged. The regression test requests `EMIT_MIR ...SimplifyLocals-final.after.mir`, and its expected output merely shows the fake asm body instead of an ICE. No concrete program input can make the original and transformed functions produce different runtime values under Miri: both compile with the fixed/modern compiler, and the behavior difference (compiler ICE versus emitted dump) is not observable by executing either function. Modeling the old path as a function that returns a different boolean/string, or as a `Result` error, would fabricate a return-value change not present in the PR and would not encode the actual historical rewrite. Therefore a source-grounded original/transformed execution pair cannot be validated with the fixed modern compiler and Miri.

analysis.summary: MIR pretty-printing ICE'd when dumping the fake body created for `global_asm!`: `write_mir_sig` only knew about AnonConst/InlineConst and function items, so `DefKind::GlobalAsm` fell into the `bug!` fallback. The fix treats GlobalAsm like the other non-item def kinds (emits no signature prefix). The regression test uses `SimplifyLocals` as the dumping pass and checks the emitted MIR.
analysis.originalLogic: In `write_mir_sig`, the DefKind match emitted "static" / "static mut" / "fn " for items, emitted nothing for `(DefKind::AnonConst | DefKind::InlineConst, _) => {}`, and otherwise executed `_ => bug!("Unexpected def kind {:?}", kind),`. Thus any DefKind not explicitly listed was assumed impossible during pretty-printing.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: When pretty-printing MIR for a body whose DefKind is `DefKind::GlobalAsm`, the old logic did not recognize the fake `global_asm!` body and reached the `bug!` fallback, producing an ICE instead of emitting the body without a signature prefix. The historical incorrect behavior was to classify `GlobalAsm` as an unexpected def kind rather than as a non-item pseudo-body.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs containing `core::arch::global_asm!(...)` that cause a fake MIR body to exist for the GlobalAsm definition, on a target with asm support, when MIR is pretty-printed/dumped (e.g., after `SimplifyLocals`).
analysis.trigger: Requesting a MIR dump/pretty-print of a `DefKind::GlobalAsm` body, for example `EMIT_MIR global_asm.{global_asm#0}.SimplifyLocals-final.after.mir` with a `core::arch::global_asm!` item in the input.
preconditions: The input contains `core::arch::global_asm!`, which since the referenced prior change gets a fake MIR body.
A MIR pretty-printing/dump pass such as `SimplifyLocals-final` is requested.
pitfalls: Do not assume every MIR `Body` corresponds to a function or an anon/inline const; `global_asm!` has a fake body.
The GlobalAsm case should emit no item/signature prefix (like AnonConst/InlineConst), not `fn ` or `static`.
The failure is in pretty-printing the dump, not necessarily in the `SimplifyLocals` transformation itself; the pass ID is the source-backed dump trigger.
This is a bug fix, not an optimization; the corrected output preserves the asm body and only avoids the ICE.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a `tests/mir-opt` regression test that contains `core::arch::global_asm!("/* */");`, uses `// skip-filecheck` and `//@ needs-asm-support`, and requests `// EMIT_MIR global_asm.{global_asm#0}.SimplifyLocals-final.after.mir`. Check the expected `.mir` file shows the fake body as `{global_asm#0}: ! = { let mut _0: !; bb0: { asm!("/* */", options()) -> unwind unreachable; } }` rather than an ICE. Two programs can differ only in whether the MIR dump targets a `global_asm!` fake body; the pre-fix compiler should ICE while the fixed compiler emits the expected MIR. No execution/build was performed for this analysis.
evidence: since https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/137180, `global_asm!` gets a fake body, that the pretty printing logic did not know what to do with.
-        (DefKind::AnonConst | DefKind::InlineConst, _) => {} // things like anon const, not an item
+        // things like anon const, not an item
+        // `global_asm!` have fake bodies, which we may dump after mir-build
// `global_asm!` gets a fake body, make sure it is handled correctly
